overhead.note: the profiler’s own CPU frames and its share of the GC pauses, taken out of every number in this report: each run loses exactly what fell inside it; the start-up scan of compiled code and the final reads sit outside the runs. The sampler’s own thread and the inspector’s are not visible from inside and are not taken out.

findings.message: Over 2462 ms the CPU was busy 33% and 25 outbound network calls took 393 ms combined.
Of the 704 ms render: load functions 19.0 ms + 365 ms waiting · other 196 ms · component render 58.2 ms · remote functions 0.24 ms + 37.1 ms waiting.

3 calls ran one after another for 111 ms: GET 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/pricing, GET 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/inventory, timer · rows (routes/hell/+page.server.ts:13). Started together they would cost 59.9 ms — about 50.9 ms saved.
findings.fix: Start them together (Promise.all) when they are independent; a call that needs an earlier result stays sequential.

findings.message: 16 calls to 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/product/:id — one per item, 112 ms together.
findings.fix: Batch them: one request with the ids (or a bulk endpoint), or fetch the list with its children included.

findings.message: Biggest CPU consumer: @ionic/core (414 ms, 52.6% of busy time).
One render of Root costs 180 ms (22.9% of busy) — most of it is formatPrice (src/lib/hell/util.ts:32), 58.1 ms.
findings.fix: Compute the expensive part once (in load, or a per-request cache) and pass the result as a prop, or render it in a deferred hole.

findings.message: ds.render ran 150 times in one render (renderOne (lib/hell/ds-ssr.ts:136)), together: 165 ms of wall for 15631 ms of summed work, 98.7 ms each. Most of it is tag ion-badge: 98 of them, 164 ms of wall (7816 ms summed).
findings.fix: They already overlap, so batching gains little: the cost is each one (make it cheaper, or cache it) and how many there are (render fewer).

findings.message: ds.pass took 166 ms of the render (ds_ssr (lib/hell/ds-ssr.ts:225)).
findings.fix: The profiler cannot see inside it — this is the wait to take to whoever owns that service, or to cache.

findings.message: ds.render.all took 165 ms of the render (processDsTagsFast (lib/hell/ds-ssr.ts:171)).
findings.fix: The profiler cannot see inside it — this is the wait to take to whoever owns that service, or to cache.

findings.message: stock.lookup ran 16 times in one render (load (routes/hell/+page.server.ts:79)), 113 ms together, 7.02 ms each. Most of it is key P0: 1 of them, 7.61 ms of wall.
findings.fix: Once per item is the N+1 shape: batch it (one call for all the ids), or fetch the parent with its children included.

findings.message: ogygia added 11.9 ms to the render: 52 islands, seed 255 KB, props 126 KB, remote seed 164 B.
The page seed is 255 KB: an island reads $page, so that much of page.data ships to the browser and is serialized on every render.
findings.fix: Read only the keys the island needs (page.data.x, not page.data) so seed shaping trims it, or pass the values as props.

findings.message: PriceTicker, ProductCard read page.data whole, so every key ships in the seed (255 KB, the biggest is catalog at 225 KB).
findings.fix: Read the keys by name (page.data.catalog, not a spread or a loop over page.data) so seed shaping can drop the rest, or pass the values in as props.

findings.message: The seed (255 KB) left the JSON lane because of catalog.facets (Map) — devalue writes and revives it several times slower than JSON.parse.
findings.fix: Send that value as a plain string or number (a Date as toISOString(), a Map as an object), or keep it out of page.data.

findings.message: MegaHeader's props (111 KB) use devalue because of config.updated (Date).
findings.fix: JSON props parse on the fast lane in the browser: pass the value as a string or number, or derive it inside the island.

findings.message: ProductCard has 48 copies on the page, each waking on visible with its own 80 B of props.
findings.fix: One island around the list hydrates once; or wake: 'interaction' so a copy pays only when touched.

findings.message: routes/hell/+page.server.ts started only after routes/hell/+layout.server.ts finished (65.6 ms later) — Kit runs a page load and its layout loads together unless the page awaits parent().
findings.fix: Move the await parent() below the page's own fetches (start them first, await parent() after), or pass what the page needs some other way — the two loads then overlap.

findings.message: routes/hell/+layout.ts is a universal load: on this render it waited 24.8 ms on calls. On a page with the client router it runs again in the browser on every navigation, and its data must be serializable.
findings.fix: If it only needs the server (a database, a secret, a private API), rename it +layout.server.ts and the browser never runs it.

findings.message: ProductCard (island host) renders 48 ProductCard rows per render, 42.1 ms together (0.88 ms each).
findings.fix: The list is the cost, not the row: page it, window it, or defer the part below the fold into a hole.

findings.message: GET 127.0.0.1:4181/hell/api/session waited 45.5 ms; its own Server-Timing says SvelteKit render 45.3 ms, postgres 31.0 ms, render 9.00 ms — 85.3 ms of the wait is on their side, 0.00 ms is the network and their framework.
findings.fix: The wait is theirs: take the biggest entry to whoever owns that service, or cache the response.

findings.message: 2 hot functions sit on one path under priceTable: formatPrice, currencySymbol — 84.0 ms together (10.7% of busy).
findings.fix: Fix priceTable once — call it less, cache what it computes, or move it out of the render — rather than each function on its own; the graph under "Paths to fix" shows the chain.

findings.message: 8 hot functions sit on one path under ProductCard: Icon, escape_html, plural, structuredClone and 4 more — 26.9 ms together (3.4% of busy).
findings.fix: Fix ProductCard once — call it less, cache what it computes, or move it out of the render — rather than each function on its own; the graph under "Paths to fix" shows the chain.

findings.message: 10.7 ms of the 48.3 ms of GC is the garbage (anonymous) (called from computeMode (hydrate/index.mjs:2042)) makes: 149 MB of the 670.3 MB allocated in the window (22%), across the window's 25 pauses.
findings.fix: Allocate less there: reuse the object between calls, avoid a clone or a JSON round trip of a large value, build strings once instead of in a loop. Most of it is churn: the heap did not grow with it.

findings.message: The event loop stalled up to 179 ms (p99) — long synchronous work blocks every other request.
Memory grew 119 MB during the window.
379 ms of busy time is the profiler itself — a one-time cost when recording starts. Your app did not pay this outside the recording.
